# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment

The incumbent passes simulation, with 307 LUTs, 281 FFs, 7 DSP48s and 0 BRAMs, but misses the 6.667 ns timing target: routed setup WNS is −8.553 ns while hold WHS is +0.075 ns. The critical path runs from a DSP48 product through rounding and saturation logic to `data1`, with 12 logic levels. The first goal is timing recovery; LUT reduction is secondary until setup and hold both pass.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the 28-bit rounding addition and post-rounding comparisons with an exact 17-bit rounded quotient and compact signed-range detection will shorten the DSP-to-`data1` path without changing transfer timing or arithmetic results.

## Instruction for generator

In `fir16_sym_core`, replace `(acc + 28'sd1024) >>> 11` with the exact identity `acc[27:11] + acc[10]`, using a signed 17-bit quotient; the discarded lower bits affect round-half-up only through bit 10. Replace the wide comparisons against ±32767/−32768 with signed 17-bit range detection and the same 16-bit saturation outputs, preserving all in-range quotient bits. Keep the five elastic slots, history update on accepted transfers, synchronous reset behavior, registered outputs, and top `// @latency 5` annotation unchanged.
